IncidentBot: PAGER: High error rate - SRV lookup timeouts observed from model-serving in eu-central-1b. Paging SRE on-call. https://ops.redwood.internal/inc/1738850123 :rotating_light:

maria (sre-oncall): ack, I’m on it. putting a bridge up in 2m. anyone seeing customer-facing errors?

chris (model-serving): yep, we started seeing 502/504s from the worker pool around 03:01 UTC. traces show request stall at service discovery layer (SRV lookup).

raj (eng-runtime): looking at runtime metrics — dns_query_latency p50 jumped from 5ms -> 250ms for queries to consul-proxy in eu-central-1b. KV cache hit rate dropped.

ana:not a scheduled outage, right? (typo)

ana -> ana (netops): can you check AZ peering / egress path for eu-central-1b?

ana (netops): hitting network graphs now. seeing increased packet drops on egress fabric for that AZ at 03:00-03:05. potential route flap to our resolver cluster in us-west-2. investigating with cloud provider.

raj (eng-runtime): dumping coredns logs from affected node pool:
```
2026-02-12T03:02:11Z coredns[1234]: [ERROR] plugin/forward: lookup _service._tcp.namespace.svc.cluster.local: dial udp 10.0.0.2:53: i/o timeout
2026-02-12T03:02:12Z coredns[1234]: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address
... stacktrace ...
```
We have occasional panics in coredns process around same window.

chris (model-serving): internal healthcheck for worker nodes failing with 'srv_lookup_timeout' which triggers eviction; backlog builds and then 502s. Customer impact: transactional inference requests are intermittently failing for ~8% of requests in that region.

maria (sre-oncall): severity -> Sev2 for now (regional customer impact). Bridge: https://call.redwood.internal/bridge/1738850123. oncall rotation: @sre-rotation you’re up for handoff in ~30m?

sre-rotation: I’ll join bridge and take mid-shift.

ana (netops): cloud provider confirms a transient route programming failure on the AZ egress gateway causing UDP loss to our resolver endpoints. They’re rerouting; ETA 15-20m.

raj (eng-runtime): mitigation plan: 1) restart coredns daemonset on affected AZ to clear panic states 2) temporarily increase client-side DNS timeout & retry in runtime (from 200ms -> 800ms) 3) enable sticky fallback to resolver replicas in eu-central-1a for SRV lookups via runtime routing policy.

chris (model-serving): starting rollout of client timeout change to worker pool now (flagged low-risk). will monitor error rate.

maria (sre-oncall): go ahead with coredns restart after confirming graceful drain windows. use this command:
```
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/coredns --selector=az=eu-central-1b
```
Execute one node at a time, wait 45s, verify no crashloops.

raj (eng-runtime): restarting coredns pods one-by-one now. watch logs for panic recurrence.

(5m later)

raj (eng-runtime): restarted all coredns instances in eu-central-1b. no new panics in logs for 3m.

ana (netops): cloud provider reports reroute applied at 03:18 UTC. UDP loss dropping to normal.

chris (model-serving): after client timeout increase + coredns restart, 502/504s dropped from 8% -> 1.2%. still some small tail.

maria (sre-oncall): recommended next steps: - keep client timeout tweak for 1h and monitor - add runtime routing rule to avoid eu-central-1b resolver until provider confirms stable for 6h - schedule deep post-incident analysis with eng-runtime + netops.

raj (eng-runtime): I’ll open a postmortem ticket and attach logs/metrics: https://pm.redwood.internal/incidents/1738850123-pm. Will also propose adding a guard in coredns runbook to auto-restart on panic and increase local cache TTL for SRV queries.

ana (netops): coordinating with provider to get root cause: seems control-plane route push had a transient error while they were rolling an egress config. They’ll share postmortem.

sre-rotation: I’ll own the next handoff; maria you can sign out after we confirm 1h of stable metrics. Recording handoff notes in bridge.

maria (sre-oncall): thanks everyone. update on customer comms: support -> draft status: "We experienced intermittent request failures in EU-Central for a small subset of customers between 03:00-03:20 UTC due to service discovery resolution issues. Systems have recovered; our team is investigating root cause." Will publish once PM ticket is created.

console-bot: Route policy change applied: failover-resolver -> eu-central-1a for service-discovery (applied by raj).

raj (eng-runtime): monitoring looks stable. sending follow-up alerts to sigs if we see >2% error rate reoccur.

(End of thread)
